request.spec:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every ROLLUP and TOTALS audit line now ends with `overdue-total=…`, and a change that only moves someone's overdue-total also writes those lines. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all on the server, in the rollup code that writes these lines:

- **Working out the figure** (`rollup/RollupService.java`): a person's overdue-total adds up the dues of their counting claims that are overdue — OPEN or PENDING with a due-by before the sheet's today. Late charges are included, n/a dues are skipped and the sheet's cap isn't applied. This is the same rule the screen uses for `person-overdue-total`. The sheet's overdue-total adds up everyone's.
- **Overdue check** (`claim/Claim.java`): a new `overdue(today)` method on the claim does that check.
- **The figures** (`rollup/Rollup.java`): each person and the sheet now carry an overdue-total. A person counts as changed when their overdue-total moves, even if claimed and due-total didn't.
- **Writing the lines** (`rollup/AuditRollup.java`): the field goes at the end of both lines. A TOTALS line is now written when any of its three totals moved.

Changing the sheet's today already took a "before" snapshot and ran the rollup audit, so it didn't need new wiring. When a new today makes a claim overdue, or stops one being overdue, the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines are now written.

There was no front-end or database change, since the screen already showed the overdue figures.
